minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard the town manager's five-year forecast, which shows a deficit, and reviewed a draft capital policy.
minutes.summary: The town manager presented the five-year financial forecast: revenue, state aid, health insurance, roads, capital and the budget calendar. The committee approved two sets of minutes and took committee reports. It then reviewed a draft capital policy, including when to borrow for big items such as fire trucks, and discussed the January and February schedule.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment at the start; none offered.

A speaker thanked the town manager. He said a projected deficit is the normal starting point each year, and that the school building project is funded outside the operating budget by a debt exclusion.

votes.motion: Approve minutes of the September 26th meeting
Approve minutes of the November 14th meeting

budget_items.what_was_said: The forecast assumes a three and a half percent increase for the schools, citing special education and health insurance risk.
The forecast assumes a rise in the Monty Tech assessment. A minimum contribution increase will be billed in FY15.
Worcester Regional gave an unofficial FY15 assessment increase, much larger than the usual yearly rise.
Expenditure assumptions outpace revenue and produce a deficit in FY15, growing over the forecast.
The town's health insurance budget is projected lower in FY15 because of retiree plan savings.
The town manager proposes raising local road funding in steps as non-exempt debt falls off.
The forecast assumes more capital funding than the past half million, but that still won't cover the priority A list.
A member asked about the gap between the amount first announced and the amount received. The town manager does not expect the rest.

decisions.decision: The town manager was asked to propose a draft budget calendar, including a presentation date, for the first January meeting.
A member will bring the free cash section and a first draft of the borrowing section of the fiscal policies to the January 9th meeting.
A follow-up discussion of the five-year forecast and budget opportunities will be put on a January agenda.

what_happened.line: The town manager presented a five-year forecast in which expenditure assumptions outpace revenue, producing a deficit in FY15 that grows over the forecast.
The forecast assumes a school increase, a higher Monty Tech assessment and a much larger unofficial retirement assessment, while health insurance is projected lower in FY15.
The town manager proposed raising local road funding in steps from the operating budget as non-exempt debt falls off, and assumed more capital funding than in the past.
The committee reviewed a draft capital policy, including when to borrow for large items such as fire trucks, and reached no resolution.
The town manager was asked to bring a draft budget calendar to the first January meeting, and a member will bring a first draft of the borrowing section on January 9th.

why_it_matters: The forecast shows spending pressures from schools, Monty Tech, retirement and roads outrunning revenue, which shapes how much the town budget, mostly taxes, may need to rise or be trimmed in FY15.
The capital and borrowing policy under drafting will guide how the town pays for big purchases such as fire trucks and road work, which affects future debt and tax bills.
